title: CDIF Provenance
description: Building block that defines the prov:wasGeneratedBy property for CDIF metadata records. Wraps the cdifProvActivity building block as an array of provenance activities that describe how the described resource was generated.

items.description: uri for specifications that this metadata record conforms to

prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Provenance activities describing how the resource was generated, including agents, instruments, methodology, temporal bounds, and action chaining.

items.title: CDIF Provenance Activity
items.description: Extended provenance activity building block for CDIF -- the schema.org implementation. Extends the minimal prov:Activity (generatedBy) with schema.org Action properties for agents, instruments, inputs and outputs, methodology and plan, temporal bounds, action chaining, and more. What the activity used is recorded with schema:instrument (instruments, software, reagents) and schema:object (inputs), not with prov:used.

allOf.title: Activity that generated the resource (CDIF core)
allOf.description: The CDIF core definition of a prov:wasGeneratedBy value: a prov:Activity whose prov:used items are strings or @id references. Any further structure belongs to the profiles that extend it (cdifProvActivity for the schema.org implementation, provActivity for the PROV-O one), which may only narrow it.

@type.description: Must include prov:Activity. Stated as "contains" rather than a single value so an extending profile can add types (cdifProvActivity adds schema:Action).

prov:used.description: Entities the activity used. Optional. Each item is a string (an IRI or a free-text name) or an object that identifies the entity by @id. The @id reference is deliberately NOT sealed: an extending profile may describe the entity in place as long as it keeps the @id, and a profile that wants only bare references can seal it itself. Role-keyed wrappers (an object whose key names a role, with no @id) are not accepted; in the schema.org implementation what an activity used is recorded with schema:instrument and schema:object instead.

anyOf.description: an IRI or a free-text name of the entity used
an entity used, identified by @id; it may also be described in place

@type.description: Must include both schema:Action and prov:Activity (prov:Activity required by base generatedBy schema)

prov:used.description: Not used by this profile. A prov:used a record carries is accepted when it passes the core shape in generatedBy (strings and @id references) and is checked by nothing more. Record instruments, software and reagents with schema:instrument, and inputs with schema:object.

schema:instrument.description: Instruments, software and reagents the activity used. Each item is either an {@id} reference to a thing described elsewhere, or a description in place whose schema:additionalType carries exactly one of three Wikidata terms (as the Wikidata entity IRI https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q..., or a wd: CURIE bound to it), which says what kind of thing it is and selects the shape it must have: https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q3099911 (measuring instrument) -> Instrument; https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q7397 (software) -> Software; https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q2356542 (chemical reagent, used here for reagents and reference materials) -> Reagent. The kind is read from additionalType, not @type, because a reagent can be a schema:Product just as an instrument is. Always an array: one activity commonly uses several (a laser ablation cell plus the ICP-MS it feeds, the acquisition software, the standards).

anyOf.description: reference to an instrument, software or reagent described elsewhere

An instrument, software or reagent described in place. schema:additionalType must carry exactly one of the three kind terms; the kind then pins the shape. A domain profile adds its own properties (a role, a version, settings).

oneOf.description: schema:additionalType names the Wikidata measuring-instrument term
schema:additionalType names the Wikidata software term
schema:additionalType names the Wikidata chemical-reagent term

if.description: schema:additionalType names the Wikidata measuring-instrument term

then.title: Instrument Description
then.description: Schema for describing laboratory instruments and instrument systems. Supports ownership, manufacturer, model, commissioning dates, hierarchical sub-components via schema:hasPart, and domain-specific typing. Instruments may be standalone devices or complex systems with sub-components.

@id.description: Persistent identifier URI for this instrument metadata record.

@type.description: Must include schema:Product. schema:Thing is allowed but no longer required -- Product is a subclass of Thing, so it adds nothing. May include additional types.

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific type classifications. Should include a scientific instrument type URI (e.g. wd:Q3099911 for Wikidata scientific instrument).

schema:description.description: Text description of this instrument, its purpose, and capabilities.

schema:alternateName.description: Alternate name(s), e.g. specific make/model designation, common abbreviation.

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier(s) for this instrument. Use PropertyValue for structured identifiers (e.g. PIDINST, serial number, inventory number).

schema:url.description: Landing page URL for this instrument.

schema:model.description: Product model information for this instrument.

schema:category.description: Instrument type classification(s) from a controlled vocabulary.

schema:contributor.description: Agents associated with this instrument in specific roles (e.g. operator, custodian, principal investigator). Use schema:owner for the owning organization.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Instrument-specific properties (measured variables, detection limits, calibration information, operating parameters, etc.). On a procedure / plan instrument (e.g. an instrument named directly on an ada:TAPPDefinition) these are schema:PropertyValueSpecification parameter templates (an overridable default); on an analysis-event instrument (an activity's schema:instrument) they are schema:PropertyValue concrete values. The JSON Schema accepts both; a profile SHACL rule pins which form applies in which context.

anyOf.title: additionalProperty PropertyValueSpecification
anyOf.description:
A parameter specification (an overridable default) declared on a procedure / plan instrument, typed schema:PropertyValueSpecification; the default sits in schema:defaultValue. Contrast with AdditionalProperty (schema:PropertyValue), the concrete-value form carried by an analysis-event instrument.
Until 2026-10-09 this declared only '@type' and schema:name, so the description named schema:defaultValue as the point of the shape while the schema did not declare it. The object is open, so nothing failed -- 203 entries in geochemBuildingBlocks carried a default that no schema described, and a placement path ending in schema:defaultValue could not be told from a misspelling.
A domain profile adds its own keys here (geochemBuildingBlocks carries ada:dataType and ada:fieldScope on every one of these entries). Those stay out of this block: it is a generic schema.org shape with several consumers, and only the schema.org properties are its to declare.

schema:valueName.description: Machine-readable name for the parameter, for serialization and for binding a form control to it.

schema:defaultValue.description: The overridable default this specification carries -- the value that applies unless the analysis overrides it. Left untyped: a default may be a string, a number or a boolean, and which one is a property of the parameter rather than of this shape.

schema:value.description: A value fixed by the procedure, where the parameter is NOT overridable. Both keys are declared because both occur: measured across the geochemBuildingBlocks corpus on 2026-10-09, of 369 PropertyValueSpecification entries under schema:instrument, 203 carry schema:defaultValue and 166 carry schema:value. A specification that pins a value rather than defaulting one is still a specification.

schema:description.description: Guidance text for the parameter, e.g. shown beside a form control.

@id.description: Identifier for this specification, so a recorded value elsewhere can reference the parameter it instantiates.

schema:validThrough.description: Date the instrument was decommissioned (ISO 8601). Absent if still operational.

schema:hasPart.description: Sub-components of this instrument system. Each item is either an inline instrument description or an @id reference.

anyOf.description: A sub-component of an instrument system. Uses the same structure as the parent instrument but without nesting (single level of hasPart).

@type.description: Must include schema:Product (as the parent instrument does) or schema:Thing (accepted for existing components).

anyOf.title: additionalProperty PropertyValueSpecification
anyOf.description:
A parameter specification (an overridable default) declared on a procedure / plan instrument, typed schema:PropertyValueSpecification; the default sits in schema:defaultValue. Contrast with AdditionalProperty (schema:PropertyValue), the concrete-value form carried by an analysis-event instrument.
Until 2026-10-09 this declared only '@type' and schema:name, so the description named schema:defaultValue as the point of the shape while the schema did not declare it. The object is open, so nothing failed -- 203 entries in geochemBuildingBlocks carried a default that no schema described, and a placement path ending in schema:defaultValue could not be told from a misspelling.
A domain profile adds its own keys here (geochemBuildingBlocks carries ada:dataType and ada:fieldScope on every one of these entries). Those stay out of this block: it is a generic schema.org shape with several consumers, and only the schema.org properties are its to declare.

schema:valueName.description: Machine-readable name for the parameter, for serialization and for binding a form control to it.

schema:defaultValue.description: The overridable default this specification carries -- the value that applies unless the analysis overrides it. Left untyped: a default may be a string, a number or a boolean, and which one is a property of the parameter rather than of this shape.

schema:value.description: A value fixed by the procedure, where the parameter is NOT overridable. Both keys are declared because both occur: measured across the geochemBuildingBlocks corpus on 2026-10-09, of 369 PropertyValueSpecification entries under schema:instrument, 203 carry schema:defaultValue and 166 carry schema:value. A specification that pins a value rather than defaulting one is still a specification.

schema:description.description: Guidance text for the parameter, e.g. shown beside a form control.

@id.description: Identifier for this specification, so a recorded value elsewhere can reference the parameter it instantiates.

anyOf.description: Reference to a sub-component defined elsewhere.

schema:relatedLink.description: Links to related resources (manuals, datasheets, calibration records, related instruments), each naming how the target relates to the instrument. Uses the same linkRole block as cdifCore; before 2026-09-23 this property was a labeled link here and a LinkRole there.

items.description:
A typed link, implemented as a schema.org LinkRole: schema:linkRelationship names how the target relates to the subject, and schema:target carries the EntryPoint actually being linked to.
This is the right shape when the relationship itself is the point -- "this is the canonical version of", "this is the download endpoint for". Where the value is simply a work at a URL, such as a license or a terms-of-service document, use schemaorgProperties/labeledLink instead: a licence is a work, not a role, and wrapping it in a Role forces every consumer through an indirection to reach the thing itself.
Defined here as a block rather than inline in a profile (where it lived until 2026-09-23) so that more than one consumer can reuse it. While it was inline in cdifCore, schemaorgProperties/instrument could not reach it and defined schema:relatedLink as a labeled link instead -- the same property carrying two different shapes depending on which node held it.

schema:linkRelationship.description: How the target relates to the subject, as a controlled-vocabulary value or a plain string label. Required: a typed link whose relationship is unstated carries no more information than a bare URL, which is what schemaorgProperties/labeledLink is for.

schema:target.description: The entry point being linked to. Deliberately not sealed: real targets also carry schema:httpMethod, schema:urlTemplate, schema:contentType and domain-specific properties, and JSON-LD is open-world.

schema:subjectOf.description: Catalog record metadata-about-metadata for this instrument description.

schema:dateModified.description: Date this metadata record was last modified (ISO 8601).

dcterms:conformsTo.description: Schema or profile this metadata record conforms to.

if.description: schema:additionalType names the Wikidata software term

then.description: Software used by the activity (acquisition, reduction, processing).

if.description: schema:additionalType names the Wikidata chemical-reagent term

then.description: A reagent, standard or reference material used by the activity. @type says what the material is: schema:DefinedTerm for a material identified by a registry entry (e.g. a GeoReM reference material), schema:Product for a catalogued specimen or purchased lot, schema:ChemicalSubstance for a bulk chemical.

schema:description.description: Text description of what this activity did

schema:agent.description: Primary responsible agent for this activity (maps to PROV wasAssociatedWith)

anyOf.description: reference to an agent defined elsewhere
reference to a participant defined elsewhere

schema:object.description: Input entity (or entities) for this activity. Per schema.org, the range of schema:object is schema:Thing. Accepts four shapes (1) a string URI, (2) an @id reference object, (3) an inline schema:Thing object, or (4) an array whose items take any of those shapes (used when an activity has multiple inputs, e.g. samples analyzed). Supports action chaining where the value references the result of a prior activity.

anyOf.description: reference to an input entity
Inline schema:Thing object describing the input entity.
Multiple input entities (e.g. samples analyzed). Each item may be a string URI, an @id reference, or an inline schema:Thing.

schema:result.description: Output entity (or entities) produced by this activity. Per schema.org, the range is schema:Thing. Accepts: (1) a string URI reference (action chaining shorthand to be referenced as schema:object of a subsequent activity); (2) a single {"@id": "<uri>"} object reference; (3) an inline schema:Thing (object with @type); or (4) an array of any of these forms (e.g. multiple datasets produced by this activity). Profiles may restrict the array item shape further.

anyOf.description: reference to an output entity
Inline schema:Thing object describing the output entity.
Multiple output entities. Each item may be a string URI, an @id reference, or an inline schema:Thing.

schema:startTime.description: ISO8601 date-time when the activity started (maps to PROV startedAtTime)

schema:endTime.description: ISO8601 date-time when the activity ended (maps to PROV endedAtTime)

anyOf.description: Spatial Extent description for CDIF discovery profile.  Note required prefix declaration for geoSparql ( http://www.opengis.net/ont/geosparql#) and OGC simple features (sf: http://www.opengis.net/ont/sf#)

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific type classifications for this place (e.g. facility type,laboratory classification, feature type).

schema:name.description: A place name for the location, either as a string or a DefinedTerm from a gazetteer.

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier for this place (e.g. ROR identifier for a facility).

schema:alternateName.description: Alternate or abbreviated name(s) for this place.

schema:geo.description: Either a bounding box or a point location.

anyOf.description: A point location. Point locations are recommended for data that is associated with specific sample locations, particularly if these are widely spaced such that an enclosing bounding box would be a misleading representation of the spatial location. Be aware that some client applications might only index or display bounding box extents or a single point location.

A schema:GeoShape bounding box. The geometry is described with a set of latitude/longitude pairs (in that order).The documentation for schema:GeoShape states 'Either whitespace or commas can be used to separate latitude and longitude; whitespace should be used when writing a list of several such points.'

schema:box.description: A GeoShape box defines an area on the surface of the earth defined by point locations of the southwest corner and northeast corner of the rectangle in latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The two corner coordinate points are separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian.

anyOf.description: A schema:GeoShape curvilinear trace, for resource related to a linear trace like a ship track or airplane flight line

schema:line.description: A GeoShape box defines a curvilinear geometry as a string of latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The coordinate point pairs are also separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian. e.g. '39.33 120.77 40.44 123.96 41.00 121.34'

geosparql:hasGeometry.description: Optional geographic extent using wkt geometry, see Ocean InfoHub (https://book.oceaninfohub.org/thematics/spatial/README.html#simple-geosparql-wkt). Other geometry schemes might be specified in a specific domain profile, e.g. for atmospheric, subsurface data, or local coordinate systems. NOTE that the location specified here should be the same as the schema.org point or contained within the specified bounding box.

@type.description: MUST be sf: (<http://www.opengis.net/ont/sf#>) SimpleFeature geometry type. See https://opengeospatial.github.io/ogc-geosparql/geosparql11/sf_geometries.ttl

@value.description: a WKT geometry description string, e.g. 'POINT(-76 -18)'

geosparql:crs.description: identifier string for coordinate reference system, e.g., 'CRS84'

anyOf.description: reference to a place defined elsewhere

schema:actionProcess.description: The plan the activity followed, or the procedure as it was performed. The {@id} reference form is the link to the plan (a protocol, method or workflow definition described elsewhere; CDIF defines no inline plan object). An inline HowTo is the procedure as performed; when the activity also followed a plan, that HowTo links the plan with schema:isBasedOn. One path finds the plan in both cases: prov:wasGeneratedBy/schema:actionProcess/schema:isBasedOn?

anyOf.description: A methodology or protocol described as a HowTo with optional steps

schema:name.description: Name of the methodology or protocol

schema:url.description: URL to a published methodology or protocol document

schema:isBasedOn.description: The plan this procedure was based on, when the activity both followed a plan and records the procedure as performed. A reference only, for now.

items.description: A single step in a HowTo methodology

schema:description.description: Description of what this step involves

schema:url.description: URL to documentation for this step

anyOf.description: reference to a methodology defined elsewhere

schema:additionalProperty.description: Domain-specific extension properties, typically the parameter values this run used. schema.org does not list Action among this property's domains, so validator.schema.org warns on it; that warning is known and accepted, because schema.org has no Action property for parameter values.

ObjectReference.title: Object Reference
ObjectReference.description: A reference to a node defined elsewhere, by its @id.

Person.description: schema for cdif profile of schema.org/Person

schema:name.description: string label for person that is meaningful for human users, should format consistently. Recommend 'Family Name, Given name' format.

schema:description.description: additional information about the agent or their relation to the described resource

schema:alternateName.description: other labels by which the person might be known. A list when there are several; a single label may be a plain string, as JSON-LD framing writes a one-item list.

schema:affiliation.description: if affiliation is present, value must be a schema:Organization.

schema:contactPoint.description: An email address or a contact web page (a form, an issue tracker), or both; at least one is required. Schema.org also allows telephone and postal contacts. A URL-only contact is ordinary in DCAT (a vcard:Kind with only vcard:hasURL), so requiring email made such records invalid.

Identifier.description:
Properties for a schema.org identifier (schema:PropertyValue pattern).
**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:Identifier / schema:PropertyValue is represented by a single attribute
of that class type. The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value
to be EITHER a plain string (interpreted as the bare identifier value) OR a
full schema:PropertyValue object (with explicit @type, propertyID, value).
Consumers should accept either form.

schema:propertyID.description: In this context for the schema:PropertyValue, this field is an identifier for the identifier schema, e.g. DOI, ARK.  Get values from https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ for interoperability. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}) so they participate in RDF entailment; free-label strings remain valid as strings.

schema:url.description: web-resolveable string for the identifier; host name part is location of a resolver that will return some representation for the given identifier value. E.g. https://doi.org/10.5066/F7VX0DMQ

schema:name.description: string label for organization that is meaningful for human users

schema:alternateName.description: other labels by which the organization might be known. A list when there are several; a single label may be a plain string, as JSON-LD framing writes a one-item list.

schema:description.description: additional information about the agent or their relation to the described resource

cdifConceptOrTermOrString.title: CDIF Concept-or-Term-or-String
cdifConceptOrTermOrString.description: Shared shape for a CDIF property that carries either a controlled-vocabulary value or a bare string label. Wraps cdifConceptOrTerm (SKOS-concept @id-ref, schema:DefinedTerm, or inline cdif:Concept) with a plain-string alternative used for legacy or single-word labels not yet bound to a vocabulary.

anyOf.description: A SKOS concept identified by URI, a schema:DefinedTerm, or an inline cdif:Concept. Shared shape used wherever a CDIF property carries either a controlled-vocabulary reference or an inline concept definition.
reference to a skos concept for the data type

DefinedTerm.description:
schema.org Defined Term schema.

**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:DefinedTerm is represented by a single attribute of that class type.
The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value to be EITHER a
plain string (interpreted as schema:name or schema:termCode in the default
vocabulary) OR a full schema:DefinedTerm object (with explicit @type, name,
identifier, termCode, inDefinedTermSet). Consumers should accept either form.

Note that this differs from the cdif Concept policy: a Concept (skos:Concept)
in CDIF profiles MUST be a controlled-vocabulary entry (object form or
@id-reference) — plain strings are not permitted for Concept-typed values
because vocabulary identity cannot be recovered from an unscoped label.

schema:name.description: text label for the term that is useful to human user

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description: The controlled vocabulary responsible for this keyword, as EITHER a plain URI string identifying the vocabulary, OR an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere in the document. Both forms are already in use across CDIF profiles and downstream ADA building blocks; permitting only the string form made the object form - the natural JSON-LD spelling of a reference - invalid, while this class's own union-type policy above explicitly anticipates both.

schema:termCode.description: A representative code for this keyword in the controlled vocabulary. Analogous to skos:Notation

AgentInRole.description: For more granularity on how a person contributed to a Dataset, use schema:Role. The schema.org documentation does not state that the Role type is an expected data type of author, creator and contributor, but that is addressed in this blog post (http://blog.schema.org/2014/06/introducing-role.html). see https://github.com/ESIPFed/science-on-schema.org/blob/develop/guides/Dataset.md#roles-of-people

anyOf.description: IRI reference to a Person or Organization defined elsewhere

AdditionalProperty.title: additionalProperty PropertyValue
AdditionalProperty.description: PropertyValue values required to define a soft-typed property with a value.

schema:propertyID.description: identifier or name for the property concept quantified by the values in this variable slot. Multiple values can specify the property at different levels of granularity.

@context.description: JSON-LD context declaring the skos namespace prefix. May be a single object or an array of strings and objects.

skos:prefLabel.description: Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string, a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values. Each language should appear at most once.

skos:notation.description: Classification code for this concept within a scheme (a single notation string, consistent with CdifCodelistConcept).

skos:definition.description: Formal explanation of the meaning of this concept.

skos:scopeNote.description: Note clarifying meaning and/or intended use.

skos:historyNote.description: Note about past state or use.

skos:inScheme.description: Concept scheme(s) this concept belongs to.

skos:topConceptOf.description: Concept scheme(s) for which this is a top concept.

skos:broader.description: Broader (parent) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

skos:narrower.description: Narrower (child) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

LanguageTaggedValue.description: An RDF literal value with a language tag, serialized as a JSON-LD value object.

@language.description: BCP 47 language tag (e.g. en, fr, de).
